I receive the following during UDX compilation Can't exec "/nz/kit/bin/adm/nzudxcompile": Argument list too long
answer:
The error is caused by the ARG/ENV list exceeding the allowed size for an exec call.  
Fix it by increasing the maximum ARG/ENV size (the limit can be set to any value between 6 and 1024 × 4 KB).  
Alternatively, you can work around the problem by creating a host user whose primary group is **not** “nz” and then changing the permission of the nz binary, e.g.:

```bash
chmod 4705 /nz/kit/bin/adm/nzsqa
```

Either raising the ARG/ENV limit or using the non‑nz user with the adjusted permissions will eliminate the “Argument list too long” error during UDX compilation.

question: Why does my JVMSERVER remain in a "BEING DISABLED"  state? When I try to disable a JVMSERVER it becomes hung and remains in a "BEING DISABLED" state. This also occurs when I shut down the CICS region. The CICS region ultimately has to be cancelled.
answer: The JVMSERVER stays in **BEING DISABLED** because the Java runtime cannot be torn down – the Language Environment enclave for the JVM was never created. As a result the JVM is terminated (DFHSJ0914) and the JVMSERVER cannot complete the disable operation, leaving it hung in the *BEING DISABLED* state.

question:
DFHAP1203I and DFHSR0601 with 0C1 in EQA10OSM after upgrading to CICS TS 5.2 Why is my CICS region failing during startup with message DFHAP1203I followed by DFHSR0601 after I upgraded to CICS Transaction Server for z/OS (CICS TS) V5.2? A system dump shows an abend 0C1 occurring in the Debug Tool for z/OS module EQA10OSM. 
I receive the following messages:
DFHAP1203I Language Environment is being initialized. 
DFHSR0601 Program interrupt occurred with system task III in control.
answer:
The region is aborting because the **Debug Tool for z/OS (module EQA10OSM)** that is being loaded during Language‑Environment initialization is not compatible with the CICS TS V5.2 release. When CICS starts it loads the LE, the debug‑tool module is invoked, and it generates an **abend 0C1**. The LE aborts, CICS reports DFHAP1203I (“Language Environment is being initialized”) and then DFHSR0601 (“Program interrupt occurred with system task III in control”).

In short, the startup failure is caused by an unsupported/incorrect version of the Debug Tool for z/OS (EQA10OSM) being present in the image. Removing the debug‑tool or installing a version that is supported with CICS TS 5.2 resolves the problem.

question:
BPM AppTarget startup hangs during startup 

During startup of the apptarget, JVM hangs with the following messages

[9/8/14 14:11:01:709 CDT] 0000001f wle W com.lombardisoftware.server.core.GroupCore getAllGroups() CWLND0004W - The system has been waiting for the group replication lock to be released for the last 10 minutes. [9/8/14 14:11:32:810 CDT] 00000022 ThreadMonitor W WSVR0605W: Thread "server.startup : 0" (0000001f) has been active for 654582 milliseconds and may be hung. There is/are 1 thread(s) in total in the server that may be hung. at java.lang.Thread.sleep(Native Method) at java.lang.Thread.sleep(Thread.java:896) at com.lombardisoftware.server.core.GroupCore.getAllGroups(GroupCore.java:545) at com.lombardisoftware.server.ejb.security.SecurityCore.listAllGroups(SecurityCore.java:566) at sun.reflect.NativeMethodAccessorImpl.invoke0(Native Method) at sun.reflect.NativeMethodAccessorImpl.invoke(NativeMethodAccessorImpl.java:60) at sun.reflect.DelegatingMethodAccessorImpl.invoke(DelegatingMethodAccessorImpl.java:37) at java.lang.reflect.Method.invoke(Method.java:611) ... [9/8/14 14:21:02:662 CDT] 0000001f wle W com.lombardisoftware.server.core.GroupCore getAllGroups() CWLND0004W - The system has been waiting for the group replication lock to be released for the last 20 minutes. [9/8/14 14:31:03:193 CDT] 0000001f wle W com.lombardisoftware.server.core.GroupCore getAllGroups() CWLND0004W -The system has been waiting for the group replication lock to be released for the last 30 minutes. [9/8/14 14:41:03:749 CDT] 0000001f wle W com.lombardisoftware.server.core.GroupCore getAllGroups() CWLND0004W -The system has been waiting for the group replication lock to be released for the last 40 minutes.
answer: The startup is hanging because the server’s JVM is getting stuck in a thread that is trying to log an FFDC (fault‑diagnostic) message. When that logging thread hangs, the JVM can freeze, and the condition is reported by the “WSVR0605W” warning that a thread has been active for many minutes and may be hung. In this case the hung thread is the one that is waiting on the group‑replication lock (the repeated “waiting for the group replication lock to be released” messages), and because the FFDC‑logging thread cannot complete, the whole JVM hangs during the AppTarget startup.

Recurrent RES StaleConnectionException How to prevent rule execution failing because of recurrent StaleConnectionException on ODM 8.8 Rule Execution Server?
answer:
To stop the RES from failing with a **StaleConnectionException**, re‑configure the WebSphere data‑source connection pool that ODM uses:

* **Set the “Minimum connections” value to 0** – this prevents WebSphere from keeping a connection alive just to satisfy a minimum‑pool size, which can become stale after long idle periods.  
* Ensure the **“Unused timeout”** (or equivalent idle‑time setting) is configured so that idle connections are closed before they become invalid.  

By eliminating permanently‑idle pooled connections, the RES will obtain fresh, valid connections when it needs to invalidate a ruleset or read its definition, and the recurrent StaleConnectionException will no longer cause rule‑execution failures.

question: Why SSH connections fail after upgrade to v7.5.2 and above? Why SSH connections fail after upgrade to v7.5.2 and above? The same configuration works on v7.2.
answer: SSH connections fail after upgrading to v7.5.2 and later because those versions disable a number of older, unsafe ciphers, MACs and key‑exchange algorithms by default. When the remote SSH client or server is still running a very old version of OpenSSH that only supports those now‑disabled algorithms, the two ends can no longer agree on a common set of cryptographic methods, so the connection is rejected. The same configuration works on v7.2 because that release still allowed the legacy algorithms in its default lists. To restore connectivity you must either upgrade the old peer to a newer, compatible version or explicitly re‑enable the needed legacy ciphers/MACs (via the Ciphers and MACs options in sshd_config).

question:
Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.
answer: Specify the full path to the silent response file when you invoke the uninstall. In other words, run the command with the complete pathname to MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt (e.g., setup /z"/full/path/MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" …) so the installer can locate the license‑agreement line.
